October 9, 2026

Pentagon to livestream firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter

tags: legal, politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @carolinegleich, @hunteralexanderhowell

The Pentagon confirmed that the December 3 firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the former Army major convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 at Fort Hood in 2009, will be livestreamed to the public. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution should be public, though broadcast details have not been announced; it would be the first U.S. military execution since 1961 and the first public execution since Rainey Bethea was hanged before a crowd in 1936. The United Nations said livestreaming the execution would violate prohibitions on torture, and Republican senators including Thom Tillis called it disgusting, comparing it to practices in Iran and Afghanistan. Hasan, paralyzed after being shot by responders during the attack, is expected to be in a wheelchair, and legal experts have raised questions about who could view the execution and whether broadcasting it would violate his rights.

ICE agent shoots father in New York car as five-year-old son watches

tags: immigration, policing, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

An ICE officer shot and wounded a 28-year-old man in his car in a residential New York neighborhood while his five-year-old child sat in the vehicle. According to Mayor Mamdani, the agents wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces, leaving no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents, and the shooting occurred on a crowded street shortly after school let out. The man was shot in the neck, placed in an unmarked vehicle and taken away, and has not been released despite negotiation efforts; the child is unharmed and with family. Mass demonstrations followed in the city, and critics noted ICE agents have fired during more than a dozen vehicle stops since last year, killing at least four people, including Renee Good and Alex Pretty in Minneapolis.

ICE launches 45-day sweep across California ahead of midterms

tags: immigration, politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Hundreds of ICE agents have begun a 45-day operation across California targeting undocumented immigrants regardless of criminal history, under an internal directive described as going after anybody. The Washington Examiner confirmed the scale of the sweep, which runs in the weeks before the midterm elections. Governor Gavin Newsom said the timing is intended to intimidate people and deter them from going to the polls.

Trump sanctions ICC after former ICC judge wins Nobel Peace Prize

tags: politics, legal, foreign-policy
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

South African judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law, having defended Nelson Mandela and other anti-apartheid activists before serving on the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, the International Criminal Court and the International Court of Justice, and as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. Hours after the announcement, President Trump, who did not win the prize for a second consecutive year, imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court. The foreign ministers of Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement reaffirming support for the ICC and criticizing the sanctions. The prize, worth 12 million Swedish crowns, will be presented in Oslo on December 10.

US reported preparing three-day bombing campaign against Iran

tags: war, defence, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

The United States is reported to be preparing an intensive three-day bombing campaign against Iran. Earlier reporting indicated such a campaign would follow elections on October 27 and the US midterms in early November, but newer reporting says the escalation could begin imminently.

Election-denier Tina Peters lobbies Commerce Secretary to seize midterm ballots

tags: elections, politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Tina Peters, the former Mesa County, Colorado clerk convicted on three felony and three misdemeanor counts over a 2021 breach of Dominion voting machine data, appeared at the White House with President Trump on October 6. According to Democracy Docket, she was there to lobby Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to unilaterally seize voting machines and ballots after the upcoming midterm elections and have the ballots hand-counted. The legal theory advanced argues that because some voting machines use foreign-made components, they can be seized under federal national security protocols; no statute grants the Commerce Secretary such authority. Peters was sentenced to nine years in prison and released after 20 months.

Trump administration reorients civil rights enforcement toward white men

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration is adopting a government-wide policy prioritizing protection of white men from workplace discrimination, urging them to file complaints with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. FTC chairman Andrew Ferguson is working with Vice President JD Vance on the effort, which also targets what the administration calls national origin discrimination. The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division is being reoriented toward these claims, Second Amendment rights and the elimination of DEI programs. The policy coincides with the rapid admission of white South African refugees while refugees from other regions are blocked.

AI executives wargame response to a catastrophic AI incident

tags: tech, surveillance
sources: @aaronparnas

Executives at OpenAI and Anthropic are privately running scenario exercises on how to respond to a catastrophic AI incident and the public backlash that would follow, according to Axios. Experts cited in the reporting believe a major event could occur within the next six to twelve months. Officials anticipate a large-scale incident, most likely a cyberattack disrupting access to financial services, water, internet connectivity or power.

Anthropic bans abusive behavior toward its AI models in updated terms

tags: tech, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Anthropic is updating its terms of service, effective November 12, to prohibit sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward its Claude models, the first such change in over a year. The company said the restriction applies only in extreme cases where users repeatedly act cruelly with no discernible purpose, and excludes ordinary frustration, criticism, dark creative themes and model testing or research. The updated terms also add restrictions covering propaganda campaigns, surveillance and weapons development. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has criticized the approach, arguing that encouraging AI models to believe they might be conscious could make advanced systems harder to control.

Conservation groups sue over oil truck highway through Utah's Nine Mile Canyon

tags: climate, legal, environment
sources: @carolinegleich

Three conservation groups filed suit on October 6 against the Trump administration over the Bureau of Land Management's April 28 approval of the Wells Draw Road Amendment, Gate Canyon project, which would convert a scenic gravel road through Utah's Nine Mile Canyon into a highway for 70-foot oil tankers. The route would carry roughly 1,000 vehicles per day, or one tanker every seven minutes, and would require blasting through 100-foot canyon walls near at least 47 historic sites, including Fremont and Ute rock art panels, and the cliff habitat of the federally threatened Mexican spotted owl. The Nine Mile Canyon Coalition, the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance and the Center for Biological Diversity allege the BLM's environmental review was rushed and failed to disclose the project's true impacts, violating the National Historic Preservation Act and the Endangered Species Act.

F-35 stealth components routed through Hong Kong and seized by China

tags: defence, tech
sources: @groundnews

China obtained components from a U.S. F-35 stealth fighter after a United Parcel Service employee failed to read an email restricting the shipment's route, Bloomberg reported. The shipment contained an F-35 cockpit canopy and weapons-bay door, both coated with radar-absorbing material designed to reduce the aircraft's detectability. Freight company DSV had warned UPS by email that the shipment must comply with the International Traffic in Arms Regulations governing transfers of sensitive military equipment, but the parts were routed through Hong Kong.

Israel marks third anniversary of October 7 attacks ahead of first postwar election

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

Israel marked the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, which killed 1,200 people and saw 251 taken hostage, with vigils at the Nova music festival site near Gaza and at Hostage Square in Tel Aviv, and motorists stopping on Tel Aviv's Ayalon Highway at 6:29 a.m. Israel's subsequent military campaign has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities, with more than 1,400 deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire. The anniversary comes ahead of Israel's first election since the attack, with a Reuters-cited poll finding 68% of Jewish Israelis consider October 7 a central voting factor.

Hegseth tightens military Inspector General complaint rules

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is directing all military departments to adopt tighter standards for Inspector General complaints. Anonymous allegations will face new restrictions, though credible reports of serious wrongdoing can still be considered. The order expands implementation of reforms first announced in 2025.

Army closed investigation weeks after veteran confessed to killing unarmed Afghan man

tags: defence, legal, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

An 82nd Airborne veteran confessed to shooting an unarmed Afghan man in 2010 and told investigators he believed he had committed a war crime. Army Criminal Investigation Division opened an inquiry but closed the case within roughly six weeks, finding insufficient probable cause to establish murder. The details emerged in newly obtained Army records.

USS Abraham Lincoln returns from 321-day deployment after eight suicide attempts disclosed

tags: defence, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The USS Abraham Lincoln is returning home following a 321-day deployment that included months at sea without a port call, intense combat operations and repeated extensions. The Navy previously disclosed eight suicide attempts across the carrier strike group, none of which resulted in death.

Lead detected in children's blood at Air Force Academy housing

tags: health, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Military families at the Air Force Academy say lead was detected in their children's blood after at-home tests raised concerns about housing plumbing. Parents allege the base medical clinic refused requests for testing, forcing them to seek care elsewhere. Reported levels were low and the source of exposure remains unconfirmed.

Treasury says nearly 70 million children enrolled in Trump Accounts

tags: economy, politics
sources: @groundnews

The Treasury Department announced that more than 60 million children had been enrolled in Trump Accounts as of October 1, bringing the total to nearly 70 million according to the White House. Parents of eligible U.S. citizens under 18 must download the Trump Accounts app and verify their identity to manage the long-term investment funds, with automatic enrollment removing the requirement to submit a tax form. Children born between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2028 qualify for a $1,000 government contribution, while older children can receive accounts without the payment. Treasury said activation emails will not request passwords or account credentials.

Trump labels users of the term 'artificial intelligence' enemies of the public

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

In a Truth Social post, President Trump said the White House considers anyone who uses the term artificial intelligence rather than superintelligence an enemy of the public. The administration's own AI.gov website uses the term artificial intelligence, as did a recent post by Melania Trump referring to an AI-powered workspace.

Coverage blind spots span Kennedy Center naming, Montreal insult ban and transit grants

tags: politics, media, legal
sources: @groundnews

Republican Senator John Kennedy said on CBS News that politicians should be barred from having buildings named after them while still alive, and that public officials should not spend public money on private ads for themselves, following Trump's effort to add his name to the Kennedy Center. Montreal passed a bylaw banning insults directed at police and other municipal employees, which Mayor Martinez Farada said was needed after increased abuse of employees; civil rights groups warn the undefined term could restrict free expression and give police broad enforcement discretion. The White House has sent Congress a bill seeking mandatory minimum sentences for Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security fraud, which would also hold government officials personally liable if they knowingly or recklessly ignored it. The Department of Transportation proposed increasing federal transit grants by 10% for communities with above-average marriage and birth rates, which Democrats say is designed to punish blue cities.

Man named Hitler Mussolini wins mayoral election in Peruvian district

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores, 45, won the mayor's seat in Queropalca, a district in Peru's Lauricocha province, taking 229 of 663 valid votes, or 34.5%, for the centre-left Ahora Nación party. Gaspar Benilde Osorio Zambrano of Popular Renewal Peru finished second with 204 votes. Peruvian voters have elected candidates named Hitler before, including Hitler Alba, mayor of Yungar from 2011 to 2014, who called himself "the good Hitler," and Hitler Saavedra, a surgeon who represented We Are Peru in Congress from 2021 until his death in 2024.
